selected_primary_idea.title: Causal Multiscale Consciousness Atlas
selected_primary_idea.one_sentence: Map the causal substrate of conscious experience with report-matched and no-report conditions, multiscale recordings, targeted perturbations, and preregistered cross-theory predictions, while separately stress-testing the molecular bridge proposed by Orch-OR.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: Distributed human brain dynamics supporting conscious perceptual experience, with a molecular submodule used only to test an explicit Orch-OR prediction.
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: Conscious experience is supported by a dynamically integrated causal process whose necessary components can be localized to a spatiotemporal network and whose signatures remain partially report-independent; the best theory will predict the joint perturbational, effective-connectivity, complexity, and no-report pattern out of sample.

theory_predictions.prediction: late long-range broadcast/ignition beyond local sensory recurrence
causal integration and differentiation track conscious state across perturbations
posterior recurrent feedback is sufficient earlier than global report-related activity
metacognitive or precision-weighted hierarchical dynamics contribute beyond sensory recurrence
an independently measured microtubule-linked molecular/quantum signature changes with conscious state on a specified timescale

falsification_conditions: A theory fails to predict held-out condition-level data better than a flexible common null after preregistered complexity penalties.
A candidate neural signature disappears under no-report control and is explained by motor, attention, confidence, or decision variables.
Perturbing a proposed necessary component changes report but not validated no-report experience proxies, indicating a report mechanism rather than experience mechanism.
The same causal pattern is reproduced by unconscious processing or by a control perturbation, eliminating its claimed specificity.
No independent, reproducible, consciousness-linked molecular/quantum signature survives neural-network and decoherence null models for Orch-OR.
selected_primary_idea.expected_contribution: A theory-neutral causal atlas that classifies signatures as state, content, report, or mechanism evidence and identifies the earliest causal bottleneck instead of assigning consciousness to a single brain coordinate.

rejected_ideas.title: Declare the frontal or posterior cortex as the location of consciousness
rejected_ideas.reason: confuses a theory-specific correlate with a settled causal substrate.

rejected_ideas.title: Use EEG complexity as direct proof of IIT
rejected_ideas.reason: a proxy measure is not equivalent to formal integrated information or a unique theory test.

rejected_ideas.title: Treat microtubule vibration as proof of Orch-OR
rejected_ideas.reason: violates the need for an independent consciousness-linked molecular signature and decoherence controls.
